approachQuestion.prompt: Count qualifying values in many prefixes. Given an unchanged integer array, one fixed threshold t, and q valid end indices, return for each end the number of values in values[0..end] that are at least t. n is 10,000..100,000 and q is 10,000..100,000. Example: values=[3,1,4,1,5], t=3, ends=[0,2,4] returns [1,2,3]. Choose a method for this workload.
constraints: Every query uses the same threshold and unchanged array.
The q results are output and excluded from auxiliary-space accounting.
Comparisons and integer arithmetic take constant time.

options.text: Build a prefix count of values at least t, then answer each query by reading the count at its end index.
options.feedback: The fixed threshold lets one cumulative count answer every requested prefix.

options.text: For each end index, scan values from zero through that index and count entries at least t.
options.feedback: It is correct but repeats earlier comparisons; with many long prefixes it repeats comparisons already made for earlier requests.

options.text: Count only whether the value at each requested end is at least t.
options.feedback: For values=[3,1,4], t=3 and end=2, the prefix count is 2, while checking only the endpoint can return at most 1.

options.text: Count all values at least t once and return that same total for every requested prefix.
options.feedback: A prefix ending earlier excludes later values. For values=[3,1,4], t=3, ends=[0,1], the correct prefix answers are [1,1], while this method returns [2,2].

feedback.reason: A running count for each prefix is a reusable summary when many queries share the same condition.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Choose the time and auxiliary-space pair for prefix-qualifying-count. The returned q counts are output and excluded from auxiliary space.
constraints: The table stores one cumulative count per input position.
Each query reads one table entry.

options.text: O(n + q) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: One pass builds the cumulative counts and each query takes one lookup. The summary table remains live and occupies linear space.

methodReveal.title: Carry a qualifying count forward
methodReveal.description: Set count[0] to one when values[0] meets t and zero otherwise. For each later index, add one to the previous count if the current value meets t. Answer each request with count[end].
